answer.answer:
Prefabrication and offsite manufacture is the one route to safer sites that this evidence base establishes as causal: moving the work into the factory takes people out of the hazardous site operation, and the same move brings schedule compression, better quality and less rework with it. It is not free: it requires precise up-front planning and logistics, and a compliance route of third-party certification and traceability for offsite work, and it works best when the manufacturer or fabricator is in the design conversation early and the design is done for manufacture and assembly. Where people and robots must share the site, safety is handled differently, by compliance with robot safety standards and by power-and-force-limiting operation kept within biomechanical limits, backed up by workforce training; that path mitigates contact-injury risk rather than delivering site safety as such. Improving site safety is a common motive, appearing in 39 of the 50 coded cases and realising its value during structural construction, and several deployed digging, handling and drilling machines were adopted explicitly to address safety, but the record links safety to taking work off the site far more firmly than to any particular machine.

**The one asserted causal path**

Improve site safety (VA13) is a Value enabler [1], applying in the Structural Construction phase in a value-realizing role [2]. It carries exactly one inbound and no outbound dependency edges, and is activated in 39 of the 50 coded cases [3]. That single inbound edge is DEP19, Prefabrication/off-site (PR2) enablesCapability Improve site safety (VA13), on the grounds that moving work offsite improves site safety, with peer-reviewed evidence [1] [4]. Everything else attached to site safety in the retrieved material is coOccursWith, which is statistical association across cases and carries no direction.

**What the prefabrication route costs and returns**

PR2 carries 4 inbound and 6 outbound dependency edges, all listed, and is activated in 20 of the 50 coded cases [3]. Its two preconditions are the ones to plan for: prefabrication dependsOn precise up-front planning and logistics (RI14) [3], and it dependsOn a regulatory route (RI18), since a functional regulatory system for offsite compliance requires third-party certification and traceability [3], both peer-reviewed [1]. To get there: DfMA (PR9) orients the project toward offsite manufacture, and vertical or early involvement of the delivering production party (CO11) is needed because integrating manufacturing and assembly knowledge into design requires the manufacturer, fabricator or contractor in the early design phase [3]; supply chain integration (VA14) supports the offsite production line [3]. Alongside safety, the same enabler returns schedule compression (VA2), factory-environment quality (VA3) and improved quality control with fewer errors and less rework (VA10) [3].

**The on-site, shared-workspace route**

Human-robot interaction (CO6) carries 0 inbound and 3 outbound dependency edges, all listed, and is activated in 32 of the 50 coded cases [3]. It co-occurs strongly with Improve site safety (weight 28), and with Significant human involvement (RE6, weight 32) and Reduce human dependency (VA1, weight 32) [5], but correlation is all that is; its asserted edges point elsewhere. CO6 dependsOn workforce training (RI6), because human-robot collaboration is contingent on a skilled workforce, and dependsOn compliance with robot safety standards (RI18), on standards evidence [3], and it mitigates contact-injury risk (RI20) through power-and-force-limiting collaborative operation within biomechanical limits, also on standards evidence [2] [3]. So the shared-workspace path reduces a named risk; it does not carry an asserted edge into VA13.

**The machines themselves**

Of the robotics enablers the question reached, none carries a dependency edge to site safety. Robot arm (RE2) carries 1 inbound and 1 outbound edge and is activated in 22 of 50 cases [3], its outbound being RE2 enablesCapability Robotic assembly (PR4) [3], and PR4 in turn hasPrecondition PR2, since automated overhead delivery and assembly requires extensive prefabrication and unification of materials [3], which is the indirect way an assembly robot reaches safety: through the prefabrication it presupposes. Unmanned mobile vehicle (RE15) is activated in 25 of 50 cases and carries no dependency edges at all [3], and Mobile (AT9) carries one outbound edge and is activated in 28 of 50 cases [3], enabling on-site digital fabrication (PR8) via autonomous repositioning and localisation [3]. One environmental lever is worth noting despite being rare: a structured, controlled site environment such as an all-weather cover (CO12) carries 1 inbound and 2 outbound edges and is activated in just 1 of the 50 coded cases [3], where robots need environments to be much more structured and controlled before they can take over, and the all-weather cover then lets welding and assembly proceed normally in rain and amplifies productivity and process stability [3].

**Deployed record**

Three deployed processes in the context name safety as an adoption driver, though the context attaches no enabler codes and no firm to any of them. census_RXM4-5 was adopted to address safety and labor, performs digging and material handling on sitework, substructure and foundation, at technology readiness level 8 [6]; census_RXM1-3 was adopted to address safety and market, performs digging and material handling on sitework, at technology readiness level 8 [7]; census_RXM23-1 was adopted to address safety, performs drilling on the structural core and sitework, at technology readiness level 7 [8]. These are earth-moving, handling and drilling deployments, that is, removing people from specific hazardous site operations, which is consistent with the prefabrication logic but is not the same edge. No deployed case in the retrieved material is linked to prefabrication (PR2) or to Improve site safety (VA13) directly, so the case evidence supports the motive rather than the mechanism.

**Caveats on scope**

The exact counts above come from the complete dependency lookup and may be read as totals for those enablers. The co-occurrence lists are cuts: 1886 co-occurrence edges touch these enablers and only the 15 strongest are shown [3], and Robotic pickup/selection (PR15) alone has 120 co-occurring [9]
